newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan's Kyocera reports lower half-year profit.
newsitem.headline: Japan's Kyocera reports lower half-year profit.

text.p: Kyocera Corp, a maker of ceramic packaging for microchips, reported lower profits for the interim period on Monday even as its cellular phone business continued to boom.
Kyocera said on Monday that on a group basis, its net profit dropped a sharp 49.7 percent in the April-September first half of this business year to 25.75 billion yen ($231 million).

The figure was lower than that of a year ago mainly because Kyocera posted a special profit of 38.39 billion yen ($345 million) in 1995/96 due to the listing of its U.S. unit AVX Corp on the New York Stock Exchange, the company said in a statement.
A loss posted by Kyocera's Japanese cellular phone affiliate, the Pocket Group, also dragged down group profit by 4.94 billion yen ($44.5 million), the company said.
But sales of telecommunications equipment, such as cellular phones and parts, more than doubled to 99.43 billion yen ($895 million), it said.

It sold 55 billion yen ($495 million) worth of cellular phones during the six months, and expects full-year sales of 110 billion yen ($990 million), company president Kensuke Ito told a news conference.
Kyocera's subsidiary, DDI Corp, is Japan's second biggest cellular phone operator and has nearly 20 percent of the domestic market.
"Sales of information equipment, including electronics parts, will be relatively good in the second half, although overall economic conditions are severe," Ito said.
On a parent company basis, Kyocera's current profit for the April-September half year rose five percent from the previous year to 50.49 billion yen ($454 million).
Current profit is pre-tax, and includes profits and losses from non-operational activities such as stock investments.

Kyocera's operating profit for the half year rose 23 percent from a year ago to 43.58 billion yen ($392 million). The company expects operating profit for the full year ending March 31, 1997, to jump 25 percent, helped by the continuing cellular phone boom. ($1=111 yen)
